newsitem.title: SPAIN: Catalan allies agree to back Spain's 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Catalan allies agree to back Spain's 1997 budget.

text.p: The Catalan coalition agreed late on Wednesday to give its crucial backing to the Spanish government's strict 1997 budget, designed to get the economy in shape to join the single European currency.

Joaquim Molins, spokesman for the Catalan Convergence and Unity (CiU) coalition, told journalists after a five-hour meeting with the ruling conservatives the CiU gave their blessing to the budget after getting agreement on three points.

He said the CiU and the Popular Party (PP), which needs its backing for an absolute majority, agreed the budget should work to reach European currency criteria, to overhaul financing for the autonomous regions and to make health care Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar had been confident earlier in the day that an agreement could be reached and had announced the cabinet would approve the draft on Friday. The last sticking point -- health care financing -- was resolved at the meeting, allowing the CiU to grant the votes of their 16 seats for the minority PP government's first budget.
The government promised that all savings from health care funding would be funnelled back into the system to make it more efficient without cutting services.

Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said the savings would come from measures that would affect rises in the health care salary base, but he did not give any details at his brief appearance before journalists after the meeting.

The PP depends on support from the Catalan nationalists and at least the four votes of the Canary Islands coalition to get an absolute majority in Congress, where it has 156 seats and needs at least 175 votes.
The Canary Islands group gave a guarantee of its support earlier on Wednesday in exchange for more investment funding being directed toward the islands.
